**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name: Eleanor Vance
Age/Gender: 80/Female
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with multiple discharges and readmissions)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Suspected colorectal cancer with anemia and abdominal pain.
Discharge Diagnosis: Stage II colon adenocarcinoma; anemia; postoperative ileus (resolved);  mild dehydration (resolved).


**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Acute onset abdominal pain, fatigue, and progressively worsening anemia over the past month.
Interventions: Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), abdominal X-ray, CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis.
Findings/Results: CBC revealed severe anemia (Hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL),  CMP showed mild electrolyte imbalance. Abdominal X-ray showed no acute obstruction. CT scan showed a large (6cm) mass in the sigmoid colon with evidence of regional lymphadenopathy.
Treatment Plan:  Intravenous fluids for hydration and electrolyte correction,  blood transfusion (2 units packed red blood cells), admission to the surgical service for further evaluation and potential surgical intervention. Pain management with morphine sulfate 2mg IV q2h prn.


**[October 27, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Preoperative assessment for suspected colon cancer.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of imaging studies, consultation with gastroenterology.
Findings/Results: Physical exam consistent with findings from imaging.  Gastroenterology consultation confirmed suspicion of colorectal cancer.
Treatment Plan:  Schedule for sigmoidectomy with possible lymph node dissection.  Bowel prep initiated.


**[October 28, 2023, 08:00]**

Provider Role: Anesthesiologist & Surgical Team
Reason for Visit:  Sigmoidectomy.
Interventions:  Sigmoidectomy with regional lymph node dissection.
Findings/Results:  Surgery completed without significant complications.  Specimen sent to pathology.  Post-operative pain controlled with PCA pump (morphine sulfate).
Treatment Plan:  Post-operative care in surgical ICU.  NPO, NG tube placement for decompression.  IV antibiotics (Cefazolin) to prevent surgical site infection.


**[October 29, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Resident
Reason for Visit: Post-operative day 1 assessment.
Interventions:  Assessment of vital signs, surgical site, bowel sounds, IV fluids.
Findings/Results:  Vital signs stable.  Surgical site clean and dry. Minimal bowel sounds.  Slight abdominal distention.
Treatment Plan: Continue NPO, NG tube suction, IV antibiotics, and pain management.


**[October 31, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Persistent postoperative ileus.
Interventions:  Abdominal examination, repeat abdominal X-ray.
Findings/Results:  Abdominal distention increased.  X-ray showed significant air-fluid levels consistent with ileus.
Treatment Plan:  Continue NG tube suction, increase bowel rest, consider prokinetic medication (Metoclopramide).


**[November 3, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Resolution of ileus. Transfer to floor.
Interventions:  Assessment of bowel sounds, abdominal exam, removal of NG tube.  Clear liquids diet initiated.
Findings/Results:  Bowel sounds present in all four quadrants.  Abdominal distention significantly improved.
Treatment Plan: Advance diet as tolerated.  Continue pain management as needed.


**[November 7, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Oncology
Reason for Visit: Pathology report review and discussion of treatment plan.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report.  Discussion of treatment options.
Findings/Results: Pathology confirmed Stage II colon adenocarcinoma with 3/12 positive lymph nodes.
Treatment Plan:  Recommendation for adjuvant chemotherapy.  Referral to oncology for further management.


**[November 10, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Review of medication list, discharge instructions, follow-up appointments.
Findings/Results:  Patient stable and ready for discharge.
Treatment Plan: Discharge to home with instructions for wound care, dietary recommendations, and follow-up appointments.


**[November 15, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up appointment before discharge.
Interventions:  Review of medication list, discharge instructions, follow-up appointments.
Findings/Results:  Patient stable and ready for discharge.
Treatment Plan: Discharge to home.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

* Sigmoidectomy performed on October 28, 2023, by the surgical team.  The procedure was successful, but the patient experienced a postoperative ileus that resolved after several days of conservative management.
* Pathology confirmed a diagnosis of Stage II colon adenocarcinoma.
*  The patient received two units of packed red blood cells to treat anemia.


**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

The patient received intravenous fluids, blood transfusions, intravenous antibiotics (Cefazolin), pain management (morphine sulfate via PCA pump initially, then oral opioids as needed), and nutritional support.  She was monitored closely for postoperative complications, including infection and ileus.  Once stable, she was transitioned to a regular diet and prepared for discharge.  Consultations were obtained from gastroenterology and oncology.


**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:  Oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325mg PO q4-6h prn pain, Senna 2 tablets PO at bedtime prn constipation,  Iron sulfate 325mg PO daily.
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with oncology in two weeks to discuss chemotherapy options.  Follow-up appointment with primary care physician in one week for wound check and general assessment.  Dietary consultation recommended.
Prognosis:  Guarded, dependent on response to adjuvant chemotherapy.  Good initial response to surgery.  The patient's advanced age is a factor in overall prognosis.

**[November 22, 2023, 10:30]**

Provider Role: Medical Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Initial consultation for adjuvant chemotherapy following Stage II colon adenocarcinoma diagnosis.
Interventions:  Detailed review of pathology report,  assessment of patient's performance status (ECOG 1), discussion of treatment options (FOLFOX regimen vs. CAPOX regimen), blood work (CBC, CMP, LFTs).
Findings/Results:  Patient reports manageable pain levels with current oral opioid regimen.  CBC shows hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, indicating improvement from pre-operative levels.  CMP and LFTs within normal limits.  Patient expresses concerns about chemotherapy side effects.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate FOLFOX regimen (oxaliplatin, leucovorin, 5-fluorouracil) due to its established efficacy in Stage II colon cancer.  Close monitoring for neutropenia, nausea, and fatigue.  Prescribe ondansetron for nausea prophylaxis.  Schedule follow-up appointment in one week to assess for adverse effects and adjust the treatment plan as needed.  Patient educated on the importance of adherence to the chemotherapy regimen and reporting of any adverse effects.

**[November 29, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Medical Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up after first cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy.
Interventions:  Assessment of treatment tolerability,  physical examination,  blood work (CBC, CMP).
Findings/Results:  Patient reports moderate fatigue and nausea, well-managed with ondansetron.  CBC reveals grade 1 neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count 1200/µL).  CMP within normal limits.  Patient's overall performance status remains ECOG 1.  Slight decrease in appetite reported.
Treatment Plan:  Continue FOLFOX regimen.  Prescribe filgrastim (Neupogen) to stimulate neutrophil production and manage neutropenia.  Adjust ondansetron dosage to improve nausea control.  Recommend nutritional consultation to address decreased appetite. Schedule follow-up appointment in one week for CBC monitoring and assessment of treatment efficacy.  Patient advised to increase fluid intake and monitor for signs of infection.

**[December 6, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Primary Care Physician
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up appointment for wound check and overall assessment.
Interventions:  Physical examination,  assessment of surgical site healing,  review of medication list,  assessment of general health status.
Findings/Results:  Surgical site well-healed with minimal scarring.  Patient reports improved energy levels compared to the previous week.  Bowel movements regular.  Appetite slightly improved.  No signs of infection.  Patient continues to experience mild fatigue and occasional nausea, but these are manageable.
Treatment Plan:  Continue current medication regimen.  Encourage continued adherence to dietary recommendations.  Schedule follow-up appointment in four weeks for routine check-up.  Advise patient to continue reporting any new or worsening symptoms and to promptly contact the oncology team if experiencing any concerning side effects from chemotherapy.

Discharge Medications:  Oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325mg PO q4-6h prn pain, Senna 2 tablets PO at bedtime prn constipation,  Iron sulfate 325mg PO daily, Ondansetron 8mg PO prn nausea, Filgrastim as directed by oncologist.
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with oncology in one week to assess response to chemotherapy and adjust treatment plan as needed.  Follow-up appointment with primary care physician in four weeks for routine check-up.  Dietary consultation recommended.
Prognosis:  Guarded, dependent on response to adjuvant chemotherapy.  Good initial response to surgery.  The patient's advanced age is a factor in overall prognosis.  Currently tolerating chemotherapy moderately well.
